text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Italy's President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro agree on the need for continuing the peace process and implementing Palestinian-Israeli peace accords. Mubarak says the Israeli government's practises are behind a recession in Egyptian-Israeli cooperation, and normalisation depends on the will of the people.

- Mubarak receives President Yasser Arafat today to discuss the latest developments in the Middle East peace process, such as the talks with the Israeli side on redeployment in Hebron. Arafat will also discuss the subject of his recent visit to Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.
- Mubarak asks for a report within 48 hours on 129 buildings which are still violating safety standards. Severe penalties are expected to be levied against negligent officials.
- 233 million pounds has been earmarked for women's health and 60 million pounds to develop hospitals and clinics in villages.
- Egypt and United Nations Development Programme to study developing the region around Al-Azhar mosque, taking into consideration the old buildings and sites of historic importance.
- Differences continue over the re-election of Boutros Boutros-Ghali in the United Nations. Talks to resume this week.
- Mubarak congratulates Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on his victory in the referendum.
